title: Staying
hookLine: Peter's words: to whom shall we go
tomorrow: a stranger walks in late. who does Jesus say he really is?

lines: LEFT THE GROUP. LEFT THE GROUP.
cards: A group chat goes quiet after someone says the hard thing. Then the little gray notices start: left the group, left the group. John's Gospel has a scene like that.
In the synagogue at Capernaum, Jesus has just said something that sounds impossible, about eating his flesh and drinking his blood. The murmuring starts: "This saying is hard, and who can hear it?"
And John says many of his disciples went back and walked no more with him. The room is emptying. Jesus turns to the twelve who are left.

teach.b: He asks them straight: will you also go away? No pep talk, no promise that it gets easier. Just the question, and the door open.

Simon Peter answers for the rest, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life." Listen to what Peter doesn't say. He doesn't say the teaching makes sense now.
He doesn't say it was easy to hear. His answer is half a question itself: where else would we go?
He has looked at the door, and he's still here, because of who is speaking, not because every word was clear. That's the Catholic picture of staying.
Not staying because nothing is wrong, and not staying out of habit. Staying because of a person. Peter's question doesn't pretend nothing is wrong; it names where he will bring what is.
Yesterday's grief and today's staying can sit in the same pew.
Here's one to tell a friend tonight: this same Peter will deny Jesus three times before the story is over, and in John's last chapter he's the one Jesus asks, three times, to feed his sheep.
Staying didn't make Peter perfect. It kept him close enough to be found again.

how: Catholics hear John 6, Peter's answer included, read at Mass; in hard seasons some pray Peter's question as their own and keep coming back to their parish.

o: sticking around out of family habit
remaining near the one you trust when it's hard

p: went back and walked no more with him
eat my flesh, drink my blood

s: everyone who heard the hard saying stayed with Jesus

staying means you have no doubts

games.q: your cousin says she's done with her parish after a bad year, but she still loves the Mass. going by Peter's answer, what's the reason people stay?
o: because of who they're staying with, not because it's easy.
because leaving would hurt the family's feelings.
because things will surely be fixed by next year.
games.why: Peter stays for a person: thou hast the words of eternal life. he never promises the hard saying gets easier.

practice: For this sit, stay put. Close your eyes and keep still, and when the itch to move or check something comes, notice it and stay.

If there's a hard place in your life right now, a team, a family table, a parish, hold it in mind without deciding anything about it. If you pray, Peter's words are there for you: Lord, to whom shall we go?

wordCard.voice: Staying. Remaining near the one whose words you trust, even on the day the saying is hard.
